claims.text: Adding approximately 3 atomic % Ag to CoCrFeNi will induce Ag surface segregation during sliding.
Sliding-induced Ag segregation will form an Ag-rich tribofilm.
The Ag-rich tribofilm will be continuously replenished as it is worn.
The Ag-rich tribofilm will remain effective from room temperature through 800 °C.
Ag atoms have sufficiently high mobility at elevated temperatures to segregate to the sliding surface.
At low temperatures, a thin Ag-rich surface layer will reduce interfacial shear strength.
Reduced surface shear strength will lower the coefficient of friction.
At high temperatures, continual Ag segregation will replenish lubricant removed by wear.
Replenishment of the Ag-rich film will counteract oxidation and wear at high temperature.
The self-replenishing Ag-rich film will minimize friction over the full test range.
The self-replenishing Ag-rich film will minimize wear over the full test range.
Ag-doped CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction than undoped CoCrFeNi at every tested temperature from room temperature to 800 °C.
Ag-doped CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than undoped CoCrFeNi at every tested temperature from room temperature to 800 °C.
Undoped CoCrFeNi exhibits variable friction and wear, particularly at temperature extremes.
The high-temperature tribological deterioration of undoped CoCrFeNi results from its inability to form a sustainable lubricating film.
Significantly different atmospheres or extreme loads may change the predicted outcome.
The proposed comparison uses undoped and approximately 3 atomic % Ag-doped CoCrFeNi under otherwise identical pin-on-disk conditions in ambient air from room temperature to 800 °C.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in both friction and wear relative to the baseline is designated as a falsifying result.
Failure to observe a continuous Ag-rich tribofilm on the worn surface is designated as a falsifying result.
